claim: The CAS all-tree model makes `uuid.txt`, `metadata_version.txt`, and `txn_version.txt` ordinary manifest tree entries, with no mutable per-part files; standalone writes and removes on committed parts use an audited manifest repoint.
A committed CAS repoint is implemented as the existing `publishEntries` sequence plus an `allow_repoint` mode on `Build::promote`, matching the modeled TLA transition `WRepoint`.
The all-tree CAS change is pre-release and does not add compatibility scaffolding; pools are recreated and ref-log and snapshot payload formats may change freely.
The all-tree CAS change must not modify `ReplicatedMergeTree` or Keeper formats.
A CAS repoint uses the standard Build path, preserving precommit-before-observe (`EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE`), and old manifests are retired by the normal GC fold without introducing a new GC invariant.
Every committed-part repoint emits `CasEventType::RefRepoint`, writes a `LOG_WARNING`, and increments a ProfileEvent.
For a ref key `K`, `repointRef` maps to `WRepoint(mOld, mNew, ref=K, w)`: one journal event in one namespace carries `old=Bind(mOld)` and `new=Bind(mNew)` under the same ref.

`Build::promote` accepts a trailing `bool allow_repoint = false`; when it is true and the committed ref names a different manifest, it emits one committed-transition RefOp from the current `ManifestRef` to the new `id.ref` and emits `CasEventType::RefRepoint`.
A same-manifest re-promotion remains an idempotent no-op, and a different committed ref still raises `ABORTED` when `allow_repoint` is false.

`repointRef(const PartRefKey &, std::vector<Cas::ManifestEntry>, Cas::ProvenanceOp)` returns false and performs zero pool mutations or events when the candidate manifest is byte-equal to the committed manifest; otherwise it publishes with `allow_repoint=true`, increments `ProfileEvents::CasRefRepoint`, logs the ref and entry count at warning level, and erases the cached folder view on success.

When `publishStaging` receives staged entries for an already committed ref, it force-freshly reads the current manifest, drops entries whose paths are overwritten, carries forward all other entries, appends the staged entries, uploads pending blobs, and publishes once through the repoint path.

`supportsAtomicFileWrites()` defaults to false on `IDataPartStorage` and `IMetadataStorage`; `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` returns true, `DataPartStorageOnDiskBase` delegates the capability, and `VersionMetadataOnDisk::storeInfoToDataPartStorage` uses one finalized and synced write instead of the tmp-plus-replace sequence when it is true.

Writes of `uuid.txt`, `metadata_version.txt`, and `txn_version.txt` follow the normal content-entry path: they are included in the initial manifest during part build and trigger a manifest repoint when written on a committed part.

`Fetcher::relinkPartToDisk` reconstructs a fetched part solely from the transferred manifest; its `part_uuid` and `metadata_version` parameters and `sidecar_values` block are removed, and the relink cookie changes from `part_manifest_v1` to `part_manifest_v2`.

For a committed content-file unlink, `unlinkFile` stages the path in `st.content_removed`; publishing filters that path from carried-forward entries and repoints unless the same transaction drops the whole part ref, which supersedes and discards the marks.

After the mutable-file deletion sweep, resolved refs contain `manifest_id`, `manifest_size`, and `published_at_ms`, while the access API is `publishEntries(dst, entries, op, allow_repoint)` and no production code retains mutable-file fields or predicates.

The MVCC atomic-write short-circuit must land before routing the former mutable files through the content path; otherwise the tmp-plus-rename sequence would require unsupported rename-of-committed-file behavior.

The freeze `metadata_version_written_by_freeze` special case is removed because an identical post-clone rewrite is absorbed by the byte-equal repoint no-op, while a differing rewrite may legally repoint.
The all-tree change deletes the `DiskObjectStorageTransaction` eager dispatch hook for content-addressed mutable-part-file renames, identified as the B182 hook.

The approved CAS codecs v3 design makes `docs/superpowers/cas/codecs_proposal_v3.md` the normative format reference and supersedes `codecs_proposal_v2.md`; `codecs.md` becomes a historical audit after `Formats/README.md` exists.
Every persisted CAS format is converted to text, including `ref_log`, `ref_snap`, and the `blob_meta` sidecar; raw payload bytes are the only binary exception.
CAS v3 fixes JSON keys to 2–5 characters, uses full-word values, and requires units to be recorded in the registry; per-object field tables are implementation-plan work under those conventions.

Every v3 CAS object has a header line `{"type":"cas_<object>","v":N}` with `v` as the only version field and gated before the body; the body is a control JSON object, sorted NDJSON records, or a raw payload zone, with a trailer for line-structured bodies.
CAS codecs use streaming `ReadHelpers`/`WriteHelpers` JSON primitives over `ReadBuffer` and hand-written deterministic writers; they do not use a DOM library.

Compression is a deterministic per-type policy of `Never`, `Always`, or `PinnedRaw` with no size threshold; `cas_ref_log`, `cas_ref_snap`, `cas_part_manifest`, and `cas_gc_outcomes` are always compressed under a `.zst` key suffix, while `cas_run` and `cas_fold_seal` remain raw.

A compressed CAS object uses one zstd frame with XXH64 checksum enabled; its declared content size is checked against the per-type cap before allocation, and a body-magic mismatch with the policy is `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

CAS integrity checks include key-to-body binding where applicable, seal-held whole-file CityHash128 verification for runs at the end of every full read, and regeneration and verification of padding zones to prevent smuggling.

Additive CAS format evolution uses a new tolerant key, while breaking evolution requires a `v` bump, `G_BUILD`/`changePoints`, and write-down-to-floor; deterministic formats use strict keys and the adoption pin to re-encode at the existing object's version on a `putDeterministicArtifact` conflict.

CAS runs use sorted NDJSON with no blocks, footer, or `seek`; `RunFileReader::seek`, `inDegreeInGeneration`, and `SourceEdgeKeyCodec::seekPrefix` are deleted because production consumers read runs sequentially, accepting approximately twice the bytes with re-binarizing `cas_run` as the localized fallback.
The optional provider-metadata mirror sets `Content-Type` per object family and `x-amz-meta-cas` to a copy of the CAS header line; the protocol never reads this metadata.

The corrected v3 inventory records that root shard `CARS` no longer exists because ref state is refsnaplog, retired set `CART` was removed on 2026-07-10, and the blob-meta sidecar had been omitted from earlier inventories.

The settled `cas_blob` header fields are `type`, `v`, `tag`, `bld`, `ts`, `by`, `op`, `ch`, and truncated `ref`; `hash_algo`, `domain_id`, `header_hash`, and `writer_version` are dropped, and the header is padded to byte 255 plus `
` while `blob_header_len` remains 256.

`Core/Formats/` may include only IO primitives and identifier vocabulary such as `CasIds`, `CasToken`, `CasBlobRef`, `CasManifestId`, `CasRefIds`, and `CasBlobDigest`; it must not include `CasBackend`, `CasStore`, or subsystem headers.
Wire structs such as `BlobMeta`, `RefLogTxn`, and `FoldSeal` move with their codecs into `Core/Formats/`, while protocol logic requiring a backend or layout remains in `Core/`.

Adding a persisted CAS object requires one `FormatId` and traits-table row, one `Cas<Object>Format.{h,cpp}` containing the wire struct, codec, and invariants, one documented `CasLayout` key builder, one shared-test registration, and one same-commit `Formats/README.md` row.

The format test harness covers round-trip, golden text, truncation at every line boundary, future `v`, wrong `type`, tolerant and strict unknown keys, critical `!` keys, duplicate keys, over-cap declared sizes without allocation, and padding or banner mutation; uncompressed bit-flip detection remains delegated to `fsck` and MergeTree load checks.

The eight-step codecs-v3 migration order is bootstrap, control plane, refsnaplog, blob meta, runs, part manifest, blob envelope, and finish; each format cuts over atomically in one commit without a dual-read arm.

Phase 1 creates `Core/Formats/` with the moved and extended `CasFormat` registry, `CasTextFormat`, a shared format test battery, and a README registry skeleton without converting any production format.

Phase-1 files in `Core/Formats/` are physically restricted to format headers, identifier vocabulary, base, IO, Common, format settings, and zstd dependencies; they must not include `CasBackend.h`, `CasStore.h`, or subsystem headers.
Phase-1 decoding maps malformed, truncated, over-cap, wrong-type, duplicate-key, and whitespace input to `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and future `v` or unknown `!`-prefixed keys to `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.

Phase-1 canonical text writers emit no whitespace outside JSON strings and terminate every line with `
`; hashes and ids are lowercase fixed-width hex strings, unbounded `u64` values are decimal strings, and bounded counts, lengths, and millisecond timestamps are JSON numbers.
`writeHeaderLine` stamps `currentCompatibilityVersion`, which equals `G_BUILD` and is 3; the `G_BUILD` 3-to-4 bump belongs to phase 2 rather than phase 1.

Phase 1 freezes `FormatId::RefLog = 19`, `FormatId::RefSnapshot = 20`, `FormatId::BlobMeta = 21`, and `FormatId::GcHeartbeat = 22`; each receives a `BASELINE` change-point ladder and none receives a legacy binary magic.

The phase-1 traits registry provides `traitsFor`, `traitsForType`, and `storedSuffix` over `TextFamily`, `KeyStrictness`, and `CompressionPolicy`, with an object cap and line cap for every non-reserved format; `FormatId::Roster` is reserved and has no traits.

The deterministic formats `cas_run` and `cas_fold_seal` are `PinnedRaw` and `Strict`, while the Always-compressed set is exactly `cas_ref_log`, `cas_ref_snap`, `cas_part_manifest`, and `cas_gc_outcomes`, whose `storedSuffix` is `.zst`.

`JsonObjectReader` is a pull cursor for one canonical JSON object: `nextKey` rejects duplicate keys, `readHex128` requires exactly 32 lowercase hex characters, and `skipUnknown` rejects `!` keys with `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`, rejects unknown keys in strict formats with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and skips unknown keys in tolerant formats.

`CasTextFormat` exposes `writeHeaderLine`, `writeTrailerLine`, `expectHeaderLine`, `sniffHeaderLine`, and `readLine`; `expectHeaderLine` validates type and compatibility without swallowing errors, while `sniffHeaderLine` returns no value for non-CAS or malformed input for fsck and dispatch.

`sealObject` compresses only `Always` formats into one zstd frame, and `openObject` accepts raw bodies but accepts compressed input only for `Always` formats, checking the declared decompressed size against the cap before allocating output.

Every v3 format registers a `FormatBatteryCase` containing an id, stored-byte encoder, decoder, and optional canonical-text golden; the battery exercises decode-of-encode, truncation, future-version, wrong-type, and leading-garbage failures.
`Formats/README.md` is a living registry whose bucket map, codec table, and evolution rules are updated in the same commit as any persisted-format change.

Phase-2 control-plane cutover converts `cas_pool_meta`, `cas_gc_state`, `cas_gc_hb`, `cas_gc_outcomes`, `cas_fold_seal`, `cas_owner`, `cas_epoch`, and `cas_mount_lease` from protobuf to the phase-1 text shape, moving wire structs with codecs and deleting each protobuf message as its codec lands.
Phase 2 uses a hard per-object cutover with no proto-then-text fallback; a half-migrated tree is acceptable because the objects are CAS-by-token or write-once and each cutover is atomic.
Phase 2 keeps `G_BUILD = 3` and adds no `changePoints` entry because it introduces no breaking text-format generation; future breaking changes earn the version bump.
CAS JSON writing pins `FormatSettings::JSON::escape_forward_slashes` to false, so slash characters remain unescaped and text bytes do not depend on ClickHouse-wide defaults.

Phase-2 JSON encodes enum values as full words, hashes and UUIDs as 32-character lowercase hex strings, unbounded counters as decimal strings, bounded integers as JSON numbers, and `UINT64_MAX` sentinel fields as decimal strings.
The shared `CasWireVocab` renders `Token` as sibling keys `tt` and `tv`, `BlobRef` as sibling keys `ha` and `h`, and maps token, blob-hash, and object-kind enums through fail-closed word maps.

`PoolMeta` is authoritative on reopen: `pool_id`, `blob_header_len`, `min_reader_generation`, and the admitted hash-algorithm list come from `_pool_meta`, while creation arguments apply only at first creation.
`PoolMeta::blob_header_len` must be at least 96, a multiple of 8, and at most 16384; `algos_used` must be non-empty, strictly increasing, and contain only valid `BlobHashAlgo` values.
`decodePoolMeta` rejects a pool with `min_reader_generation` above `G_BUILD` or a generation below `kRefSnapshotLogGeneration` with `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.

The server-root text objects are `cas_owner`, `cas_epoch`, and `cas_mount_lease`: the owner binds a server-root id to a server UUID, the epoch stores the monotone next writer epoch, and the mount lease stores the live holder and merged `min_active` state.
A `MountLease` uses `UINT64_MAX` in `min_active` as the retired farewell sentinel, and `gc_fenced` is a terminal GC fence-out flag.

`cas_gc_hb` is a full header'd text object with a header line and one JSON body line; its advisory owner and monotone `hb_seq` semantics remain unchanged, and the former 24-byte unversioned representation is removed.
`GcState.gc_shards` is immutable and must be at least 1; decoding a zero value raises `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

`cas_gc_outcomes` is line-structured as a header, one flat JSON record per `OutcomeEntry` in insertion order, and a `{"n":<count>}` trailer; it is always zstd-compressed and stored under a `.zst` key suffix.
`cas_gc_outcomes` is not deterministic: it uses idempotent `putIfAbsent`, and replay adopts an existing durable object after decoding rather than treating byte inequality as a correctness failure.

`cas_fold_seal` is `PinnedRaw` and `Strict`; its encoder emits fixed field and section order, sorts vector collections by run key inside the encoder, and must be byte-reproducible for `putDeterministicArtifact` adoption.

The `cas_fold_seal` body consists of a header, a metadata line, record sections in coverage, blob-target-runs, part-manifest-cleanup, condemned-summary, and namespace-cleanup order, followed by a `{"n":<total record count>}` trailer; record kinds are `cov`, `btr`, `pmc`, `cnd`, and `nsc`.

A fold-seal `nsc` record reconstructs its map key as `ns + newline + renderRefTxnId(remove_txn_id)`; a zero `{0,0}` transaction id is invalid for `nsc`, while a zero `last_folded_ref_id` is allowed for coverage records.

The protobuf graveyard is deleted only after grep proves that no production or test code references `cas_format.pb.h`, `clickhouse::cas::format`, or `cas_format.proto`; phase 2 removes `Core/Proto/` and the `clickhouse_cas_proto` build and link wiring because the eight control-plane objects were its only consumers.

Phase 2 exit requires all eight control-plane objects to be text, each to have a `FormatBatteryCase`, `cas_gc_hb` to be header'd, `cas_fold_seal` determinism to remain green, `cas_gc_outcomes` to use `.zst`, and `dbms` plus `unit_tests_dbms` to link without `clickhouse_cas_proto`.

Phase 3 converts `cas_ref_log` and `cas_ref_snap` to Always-compressed text, re-derives JSON-inflated byte budgets, preserves key-to-body `ns` and `txn_id` binding, and updates builders and parsers for the `.zst` suffix.
Phase 4 converts the fixed 22-byte `CasBlobMeta` sidecar to one-line JSON while keeping deduplication, resurrection, and token semantics unchanged.

Phase 5 converts `CasRunFile` to sorted NDJSON with a trailer and whole-file CityHash128 seal verification on every full read, while deleting the block/footer machinery and sequentially-unused seek APIs; the coupled `part_manifest_cleanup` fold-seal field removal depends on phase 2.

Phase 6 converts `CasManifestCodec` to a JSON descriptor followed by a `head -v` banner payload zone, verifies regenerated padding and banners, and follows phase 5 because `RunKind::ManifestEntries` and the embedded stream surface are shared.

Phase 7 converts `CasEnvelope` to a 256-byte JSON header line padded with spaces, keeps payload offset 256, removes `hash_algo`, `domain_id`, `header_hash`, and `writer_version`, and treats former TLV fields as `!`-critical keys.
Phase 8 is strictly last and covers the provider-metadata mirror, documentation finalization, and reducing or deleting `CasInspect`; protobuf build removal is already assigned to phase-2 Task 7.
